flashcards.back: Daily life in many border towns reflects this close interdependence, with vibrant markets and thriving trade.

flashcards.back: India is Nepal’s largest trading partner, supplying essential goods such as petroleum, medicines, food items, and manufactured products.
flashcards.source_evidence: India is Nepal’s largest trading partner, supplying essential goods such as petroleum, medicines, food items, and manufactured products.

flashcards.back: In return, Nepal exports agricultural produce, handicrafts, and garments.

flashcards.back: These exchanges not only contribute to economic development but also reinforce the social and economic integration of the border communities.

flashcards.back: The India- Nepal relationship stands as a unique example of neighbourhood cooperation shaped by a shared history, faith, geography, and a commitment to regional harmony.

flashcards.back: DON’T MISS OUT What is an ‘open border’?
flashcards.source_evidence: DON’T MISS OUT What is an ‘open border’?
flashcards.subject: Social Science

flashcards.back: It is when people from two countries can travel across the border without a visa or passport.
flashcards.source_evidence: It is when people from two countries can travel across the border without a visa or passport.
flashcards.subject: Social Science

flashcards.back: This enables families living on both sides to stay connected, and people to move easily for work, education, trade, or religious visits.
flashcards.source_evidence: This enables families living on both sides to stay connected, and people to move easily for work, education, trade, or religious visits.
flashcards.subject: Social Science

flashcards.back: However, India and Nepal work together to ensure the open border remains safe and is not misused; it is a symbol of trust and friendship between the two countries.
